meta.title: Інвестиційний Меморандум Cursor (Anysphere)
meta.biasNote: Underwriting/marketing material — figures support investment thesis; triangulate with public signals.

founders.name: Michael Truell
founders.bio: MIT; Neo Fellow; ex-Google (recommendation models). Youngest CEO of a $45B+ company.

founders.name: Sualeh Asif
founders.bio: MIT; IMO contestant from Pakistan. Leads product.

founders.name: Arvid Lunnemark
founders.bio: Former CTO; left to found Integrous Research (AI safety lab).

founders.name: Jordan Topoleski
founders.bio: Harvard; previously founded fintech startup ($10M+ raised). Selected from 200K candidates as Adecco "CEO for one month". Leads enterprise GTM.

competitive.name: Lovable
competitive.focus: Fastest EU startup; pure vibe-coding. 10% of apps had security flaws.
competitive.note: Sacra Feb 2026 estimate; some sources still cite $200M ARR from Nov 2025

competitive.name: Replit
competitive.focus: Browser-native, non-developer friendly. Lower enterprise penetration.
competitive.note: 2025 actual revenue $240M; company targets $1B ARR by end-2026

competitive.name: Cognition (Devin + Windsurf)
competitive.focus: Devin + Windsurf combined after July 2025 acquisition.
competitive.note: Cognition $696M + Windsurf $243M pre-acquisition; combined ARR ~$155M at acquisition, since "more than doubled"

competitive.name: GitHub Copilot
competitive.focus: Distribution moat: 90% F100, bundling. Plugin model — less codebase awareness.
competitive.note: Microsoft does not disclose Copilot ARR separately; analyst estimates based on 4.7M paid subscribers

competitive.name: Claude Code
competitive.note: Anthropic raised $64B+ total; Claude Code is a product line, not a separately funded entity

competitive.name: OpenAI Codex
competitive.focus: 2M+ weekly users; +70% MoM growth as of March 2026.
competitive.note: OpenAI does not break out Codex ARR

competitive.name: Kiro
competitive.focus: AWS-owned, successor to Amazon Q Developer; not separately funded.

features.name: Composer
features.description: In-house coding model / agent that operates on the entire codebase across multiple files.

features.name: Codebase Indexing
features.description: AI builds full project context — structure, dependencies, patterns — improving recommendation quality.

features.name: Tab Autocomplete
features.description: Real-time code prediction on Cursor proprietary model (4× faster than competitors).

features.name: Agent Mode
features.description: Autonomous: uses terminal, installs deps, fixes errors, iterates until task is complete.

features.name: Custom Rules
features.description: Teams define coding standards once — AI follows them across all projects.

features.name: Cloud Agents
features.description: Tasks run in background on Cursor servers; developer returns to completed work.

features.name: Bugbot
features.description: AI code review on every pull request ($40/user, add-on).

distribution: Freemium → Pro/Business; 36% free-to-paid conversion (vs 2-5% typical SaaS)
Bottom-up enterprise: dev → team → org adoption

deal.anton_tier_note: Research only — no position taken. Toloka offered $45B pre-money tier.

risks.label: Growth slowdown breaks the math
risks.note: At $45B entry, you need hypergrowth to keep going. If growth halves, you barely get your money back in 3 years.

risks.label: AI model makers are building rival tools
risks.note: Anthropic (Claude Code), OpenAI (Codex), Google (Windsurf) all sell coding tools now. Cursor relies on their models.

risks.label: Microsoft Copilot wins by default
risks.note: Free with GitHub, VS Code, Azure. 100M+ developers get it without choosing. Cursor has to fight for every one.

risks.label: Still burning cash at scale
risks.note: AI features need expensive GPUs. Revenue grows fast, profit doesn’t keep up.

risks.label: Founder and engineers leaving
risks.note: CTO left in 2025, key engineers went to xAI. Four remaining co-founders are 25-26 with no prior experience.

risks.label: One bad incident triggers churn
risks.note: Prompt injection, data leaks, or surprise pricing could push developers to alternatives. Switching is easy.
